title.narrative: Improved capacity of Social Security Institutions for extension of coverage and provision of better benefits for all

description.narrative: Mozambique remains one of the poorest countries in the world with almost half of the population living in chronic poverty; high rates of unemployment, HIV prevalence and stunting; and recurrent food insecurity. Economic growth has been declining as a result of cyclones, droughts, flash floods, increasing cost of living, and weak agricultural performance. Inflation has been on the rise due to tight monetary policy and the exchange rate has been stable. The ILO through the Country programme is therefore supporting development of a sustainable financing for social protection supporting development of a sustainable financing strategy for social protection to facilitate long-term sustainability of the social protection system in Mozambique. The ILO is building the capacity of government, social partners and national partners to design and deliver comprehensive social protection programmes through capacity building interventions on International social security standards and the TRANSFORM Package on Building and Managing Social Protection Floors. Further, priority has been placed on developing capacities for greater inter-institutional interoperability between social protection management information systems and contribute towards improving the governance and administration of social assistance, including statistics, monitoring and evaluation, management information systems and payment efficiency, to enhance access to and delivery of social protection benefits. The beneficiaries include Government Ministries, Social Partners, Development Partners, beneficiaries of social assistance programmes, population in active labour market (Community Members), workers in the formal and informal sectors, pensioners and Civil Society Organizations. The Partners involved are the National Social Security Institute (INSS), National Institute of Social Action (INAS), Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Gender and Social Welfare, Employers’ and employers' Organisations.
